Photograph: Blondet Eliot/Abaca/Shutterstock France National Rally’s Jordan Bardella rails at ‘war’ on party after antisemitism claims President of Marine Le Pen’s far-right party faces calls to resign over comments he allegedly wrote as a teenager Angelique Chrisafis in Paris Tue 29 Sep 2026 11.16 EDT Last modified on Tue 29 Sep 2026 11.19 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Jordan Bardella , the head of Marine Le Pen’s far-right National Rally (RN), has claimed a “total war” is being waged against his party as he faces a political storm after the publication of antisemitic comments he allegedly wrote as a young party member. Bardella, who is facing calls from political opponents to resign, said on Tuesday that the report by the investigative website Mediapart was false. To a standing ovation from his party’s lawmakers and senators at a meeting in parliament, he said the report was an attempt to damage his party as Le Pen tops the polls before the 2027 presidential election. “We are seeing the beginnings of a total war, an attempt to destabilise the presidential campaign,” Bardella said. He accused Mediapart of wanting “to kill my political career” and said he would take legal action for defamation. Le Pen, at Bardella’s side, said she had “absolute confidence” in him. Marine Le Pen hails RN senate surge as ‘milestone’ towards French presidency Read more Journalists at Mediapart said they had independently authenticated the comments allegedly written between 2013 and 2015, including in email groups and on messaging services. Bardella was aged 17 to 18 at the time and was a member of the party that was then called the Front National. The alleged comments included “the Jew has to dominate other peoples, crush them, and rob them; a Zionist is necessarily a Jew, and fundamentally so”. He is also alleged to have written “all the banks are owned by Jews”. Mediapart’s investigation has shaken Le Pen’s presidential campaign. Since Le Pen took over the party leadership in 2011, she has sought to detoxify the party image and move it away from its antisemitic past in order to increase its electoral reach. When Le Pen’s father, Jean-Marie Le Pen , co-founded the party in 1972, its ranks included former members of a Waffen SS military unit under Nazi command during the second world war. Pierre Bousquet, a former member of the Waffen SS Charlemagne division, was the party’s treasurer for its first nine years. Another early member had been in the paramilitary militia under Philippe Pétain, the leader of the puppet Vichy regime that collaborated with the Nazis and ensured the deportation of one-quarter of France’s Jewish population to concentration camps, about 76,000 people. In 1987, Jean-Marie Le Pen described the Holocaust as a “mere detail” of the second world war . In the decades that followed he was convicted more than 15 times for hate speech and contesting crimes against humanity as he repeated negationist comments, including saying the Nazi occupation was “not particularly inhumane” . Marine Le Pen, who expelled her father from the party in 2015 after he repeated antisemitic comments, has in recent years directly appealed to French Jewish voters. She said her party would protect them, describing the RN as “the best shield for our fellow French citizens of Jewish faith”. View image in fullscreen Bardella and Marine Le Pen at a rally in Lievin, northern France, in July. Photograph: Jean-François Badias/AP Bardella made an unprecedented visit to Israel in 2025, the first by a French far-right leader, in an attempt to demonstrate the RN’s new credentials. In 2023, Bardella told a TV interviewer he did not think Jean-Marie Le Pen was antisemitic, before backtracking on his comments after criticism. The French foreign minister, Jean-Noël Barrot, responding to the Mediapart investigation, wrote on social media: “To all those with a short memory: antisemitism isn’t an accident in the RN, it’s that party’s history. That’s the real face of the far right.” Aurore Bergé, the minister for equality and against discrimination, said the “antisemitic and conspiracy theory” content of the alleged messages “reminds those who might have forgotten the nature of the far right”. Raphaël Glucksmann, a candidate in the Socialist presidential primary, wrote on social media that no public relations exercise would fundamentally change the RN. “Let us never forget that they all joined a party founded by antisemitic fanatics and out-and-out racists,” he said. Yonathan Arfi, of the CRIF, the umbrella group of French Jewish organisations, told France Culture radio he was “stupefied by the virulence of the antisemitic comments” allegedly made by Bardella. He said that if true, the comments undermined the RN’s claims to have detoxified its image. He asked: “How could a political party leader, having made such sickening comments, reach such a high position in a party that claims to have changed and now fights against the hatred of Jews?” The Green leader, Marine Tondelier, said Bardella, an MEP, should resign from all his political positions. https://www.stiripesurse.ro/pm-niculescu.text: Prime Minister Luca Niculescu is visiting the Cernavoda Nuclear Power Plant on Saturday, accompanied by the Minister of Energy, Dumitru Chisalita.The two will tour the Cernavoda Nuclear Power Plant and hold a meeting with the management of Nuclearelectrica to discuss the company's operations and strategic projects.The visit by the Prime Minister and the Minister of Energy follows the resynchronization of Unit 1 of the Cernavoda Nuclear Power Plant with the National Energy System on Friday afternoon.According to Nuclearelectrica company, reactor start-up procedures were initiated on Wednesday, once the necessary minimum conditions had been met.Unit 1 of the Cernavoda Nuclear Power Plant underwent a controlled shutdown and was disconnected from the National Energy System on July 28, due to low water levels in the Danube. Subsequently, in mid-August, Unit 2 was also disconnected.The Cernavoda Nuclear Power Plant operates Units 1 and 2, each with a capacity of 700 MWe; they use natural uranium as fuel, with heavy water serving as both a moderator and a coolant. With both units in operation, SNN accounts for approximately 20% of Romania's total dispatchable power generation.

Photo shows overseas media guests visit Xiaomi auto factory in Beijing, Nov. 6, 2026. After the tour, Marcos Costa de Oliveira, editor-in-chief of Brazil's Monitor Mercantil newspaper, said he is a lover of Xiaomi stuff, and Xiaomi cars are beautifully designed and useful too. Xiaomi's greatest advantage is its ability to combine innovative technology, attractive design and impressive performance, said Tamas Kovacs, CEO of ATV Hungary. Covering an area of approximately 718,000 square meters, the factory is a modern smart manufacturing campus for Xiaomi NEVs that integrates R&D, production, sales and customer experience. The factory has upgraded traditional auto-making processes to six tailored to NEV production, with 100 percent automation achieved in key processes. More than 700 robots work in coordination across the production lines while artificial intelligence (AI) technologies are employed to significantly improve quality inspection accuracy. Advertisement "I was particularly impressed by the extensive use of robotics, automation and artificial intelligence throughout the manufacturing process," said Kovacs. "Xiaomi's manufacturing capabilities demonstrate China's remarkable progress in industrial innovation." The interactive demonstration of Xiaomi's human×car×home smart ecosystem was another highlight of the tour. The ecosystem allows users to remotely control smart home devices directly from their vehicles through voice commands or preset scenarios, enabling seamless connectivity across different living scenarios. Yasiru Bandara Ranaraja, founding director of Belt & Road Initiative Sri Lanka, said Xiaomi is very innovative and gives the whole solution of the car for controlling all electronics. Such ecosystem is one of the most innovative achievements of Xiaomi, said Kovacs. "I believe this integrated approach represents an important direction for the future of transportation." Advertisement When asked about Xiaomi's plan to go global, many guests expressed hopes to see Xiaomi vehicles sold in their own countries. Agnes Kalekye Nguna, CEO of Kenya Broadcasting Corporation, said NEV plays a significant role in environmental conservation and promoting utilization of clean energy in Africa. "Come to Africa, we are waiting for you!" The tour was one of the events held during the 7th World Media Summit running on November 5-9 in Beijing, which gathered nearly 500 guests from mainstream media, think tanks, government departments and international organizations across 112 countries and regions.
